children: The Indian rupee traded in a narrow range near 96 per dollar on Wednesday after the Reserve Bank of India's intervention limited pressure from rising oil prices and U.S. Treasury yields.
held at 95.93 per U.S. dollar at 10:46 a.m. IST, having traded within an 8-paisa range so far during the session.
The currency was expected to weaken at the open as the dollar rose ahead of the Federal Reserve's rate decision and oil prices stayed high, but RBI intervention limited losses.
The RBI has regularly sold dollars through state-run banks in recent sessions to curb the rupee's decline, while using dollar-rupee swaps to manage liquidity.
Traders said the central bank's dollar sales have not been focused on defending any specific level, suggesting it was more intent on slowing the rupee's fall than holding a specific rate.

The rupee remains on the defensive amid importer dollar demand and rising U.S. yields, with markets pricing in a more than 90% chance of a Fed rate hike on Wednesday, up from around 60% a week ago as inflation concerns grew.
Investors are likely to focus on the Fed's updated dot plot and economic projections for clues on whether another hike could follow later this year.
Oil remains the biggest immediate pressure point for the rupee. Brent is hovering near $108 a barrel.
The oil surge feeding into U.S. bond yields, with the 10-year Treasury yield having moved to near 5%, adding another layer of pressure on the rupee.
Considering the prevailing backdrop, there is a higher probability of rupee falling more, and eventually moving towards 96.30 to 96.50 level, Mumbai-based CR Forex said in a note.
